title: The Final Interview Mistake That's Costing You Job Offers
description:
If you're making it to the final interview but still not getting the offer, the problem may not be your qualifications or your experience. It could be that you're giving employers too much information instead of the right information.

In this Short, I explain why saying less can actually make your value stand out more—and how to focus your interview answers on what employers actually care about.

Subscribe for practical job search, resume, LinkedIn, networking, and interview strategies that help you get seen, get interviews, and get hired.

If you're job searching, trying to get more recruiter messages, improve your LinkedIn profile, optimize your LinkedIn headline, or increase your visibility to hiring managers and recruiters, this video is for you.

transcript: Making it to the final interview is proof that you don't need to sell yourself harder. Your resume already sold them on your qualifications. Now, it's your job to listen just as carefully as you speak. If you're making it to the final interview and still not getting the offer, the problem probably isn't that you're saying the wrong thing. It could be you're just saying too much. Most candidates answer every question with every accomplishment, every detail they can ever think of, but each irrelevant detail makes it harder for the employer to see your value. Your goal isn't to tell them everything you've ever done is to make it painfully obvious you can solve their problem. The candidates who get the offers aren't the one who talks the most, they're the ones who communicate the most relevant value. Follow for more practical interview strategies that help get you seen, get you interviews, and get you hired.
